verdicts.reason: Quote states existing blocks may be used directly without sideband signals; scenario check is fine.
Vague 'straightforwardly adapted' statement about design effort; nothing to verify or exercise. Also merely restates the second half of the same sentence as 01.

Rule is right: one request, one response per cycle, no bursts. Per-cycle structure is inherent to the protocol and bursts are indicated by the absence of burst support, so it is a scenario/feature description rather than a clean interface assertion; a MUST statement on the bus is best checked by scenario (e.g. no multi-beat transfers, size limited to one beat).
Descriptive statement about composability of primitives into a crossbar; no checkable behaviour.
Quote states interoperability of extended-spec blocks with base-spec blocks; can be exercised by a scenario mixing them.

Quote says baseline blocks ignore user signals as receiver; it is a requirement on the receiving block, and checkable as a scenario (vary user bits, observe no behaviour change). Actor should be any receiver, which is best expressed as 'any'.

Baseline source generates a project-specific default value for user signals; the actual default is project-specific, so it is not a universal interface assertion but can be exercised in a scenario. Actor is any source.
Statement that blocks can be easily modified; a design-effort remark with nothing to verify.

duplicates.reason: Both come from the same sentence and state that existing blocks can be used or adapted for the user extensions.

questions.question: What is the project-specific default value for user signals generated by a baseline source, and does it need to be a constant across the project? Is it checkable?
Does 'no burst transactions' mean a request size is limited to the bus width, or are multi-beat operations simply unsupported? Define the exact checkable condition.
